finding.claim: Big5 multibyte recognizer treats 0xFA-0xFE as lead bytes (isHead 0xA1-0xFE), but the server's Big5 lead range is narrower (0xA1-0xF9, unverified here). A Buffer parameter containing FA 5C 27 is written as FA 5C 5C 27, so the server treats FA as a single byte, consumes 5C as an escape, and the quote closes the literal (SQL injection).
finding.source: Buffer/Uint8Array value bound with ? in text-protocol connection.query(sql, [buf]) on a big5 connection charset; attacker controls the bytes

trace.note: big5.length returns 2 for trail 0x40-0x7E or 0xA1-0xFE, so 0x5C is a valid trail
writeBufferEscape bound to writeBufferEscapeMb for big5
NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES early-return not taken, so the mb walk runs
head FA with mbLen 2 copies FA and 5C verbatim, no escape inserted
following quote 0x27 gets a backslash, producing wire bytes FA 5C 5C 27

finding.guards_checked: NO_BACKSLASH branch (line 684) only; _BINARY prefix is not a control; lone-head escape (706-713) does not fire because the walker believes FA is a head. Non-big5 recognizers (gbk, sjis, cp932, gb18030) match recalled server ranges and were judged SAFE.

finding.claim: With permitSetMultiParamEntries enabled, object keys are written raw inside backticks with no escaping, so a key containing a backtick breaks out of the identifier and injects SQL. The same unescaped pattern exists at lib/misc/utils.js:213.
finding.source: Object keys of a value bound to ? when permitSetMultiParamEntries is true (opt-in; default false at lib/config/connection-options.js:132); attacker controls keys, e.g. conn.query('UPDATE t SET ?', req.body)
finding.sink: Query text written at lib/cmd/encoder/text-encoder.js:135 (out.writeString('`' + key + '`'))

trace.note: same unescaped key pattern in the connection.escape() path

finding.guards_checked: Option is off by default. Values are escaped recursively via writeParam (line 137), but keys have no backtick doubling, unlike escapeId (lib/misc/utils.js:106). No enforced control on keys.

finding.claim: pool.escape() uses backslash escaping when no idle connection exists. The loop iterates Object.keys indices against a thread-id-keyed object, so _searchInfo returns null, and escapeString then treats the server as not NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES. Under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES, the emitted \' closes the literal (SQL injection).
finding.source: Application value passed to pool.escape(userValue) while the server runs with NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES and no idle pool connection exists (all busy, or before first connect)

trace.note: lookup by those indices in a thread-id-keyed object returns undefined

finding.guards_checked: NO_BACKSLASH check exists in utils.js:249 but fails open when info is null (comment at line 248 acknowledges this). Safe when an idle connection exists, so the issue is load- and timing-dependent.

finding.claim: Server-supplied redirect string causes a new connection to a server-chosen host using the original connection's password (this.opts retained), enabled by default. Without TLS, the native-password response and client-side outbound connections are sent to arbitrary host:port.
finding.source: Redirect value sent by the server (lib/cmd/ping.js:43-44 triggers connection.js:1593); requires a malicious server or on-path attacker against a plaintext connection
finding.sink: new Connection with Object.assign({}, this.opts, redirectOpts) at lib/connection.js:1633-1634

trace.note: redirectRequest processed when not in transaction
host and port taken from server URL
user and password only overwritten if present in URL
original this.opts password and user retained

finding.guards_checked: permitRedirect default true (lib/config/connection-options.js:90); same-host skip (connection.js:1621); not-in-transaction check (1598); TLS options copied so verification applies when ssl is on; clear-text plugin requires TLS (lib/cmd/handshake/authentication.js:203). Gap is the plaintext case only.
